text:
I have a 140 pound Newfi/retriever mix. He’s thin and long/tall. He’s two, so he still plays like a puppy at the dog park and it’s a joy to see him get chased by little dogs, and when he lays down they climb all over him.

He likes to sleep under my bed which is all that spacious. So when he moves my entire king bed bounces around like there’s an earthquake. Sharing the couch with him is sweet, but cramped.

My fully grown Labrador tries to lie on our Pomeranian (unsuccessfully) and has tried to full on lie on my stomach when I need comfort. I’ve never had the heart to remind him he’s about 70 something pounds lol

Stranger: Wow, your dog is bouncy!! How old is he?
Me: 12
Stranger: Months?
Me: No, years. And yes, he’s been like this the whole time.

Portuguese Water Dogs are a trip, let me tell you.
Mine's 80 pounds and still tries to climb onto my shoulder like a parrot whenever I sit on the couch
Absolutely my 7yr old golden thinks shes a tiny pup and honestly i feel like its a good thing. Keeps her youthful and full of energy.

My 50 lb Standard Poodle loved to sleep under the couch when she was a puppy. She started getting stuck at around a year old when she was simply too big to wiggle out. I would have to lift the end of the couch and rescue her, over and over. She finally stopped trying until she was almost three, when she tried again. I heard the most god-awful caterwauling, and had to go get her out.

People will often say “puppy?” to me about my dog. He’s 5 1/2. He can be sitting there like the best neutral boy and they always ask if he’s a puppy. lol. Hitting 5 I feel like he shifted into being a mature doggy
My dog Moxy was an OEB, she thought she was a lap dog lol!

Every large dog I've ever known thinks it's a lap dog. I don't have a problem with Sergeant Pickles across my lap, but I do mind him anchoring himself with his bony elbows! Ow! His little sister fits better.

He doesn't have puppy stuff so much as he has the hound tendency to utterly forget his name if he's got a scent. She has the nickname of Miss Chew, which she comes by honestly being a boxer/staffy mix, and there's a reason that the remote control and my wireless mouse are put away in a drawer when not in active use.
When my youngest arrived at our house he could fit in the palm of my hand. Now he's 3 and 85 lbs. I still call him my leeeeeetle tiny baby 🍼 as he plops all his weight on top of me
50lb boxer pitt mix is the biggest baby I have ever met. He has no idea he isnt a lap dog. He jumps around with our shih tzu like they are the same size
My 50 lb basset hound thinks it’s okay to walk on me to get me up in the morning. Ow, my ribs!
Ours still tries to curl into the little round bed she had as a puppy and ends up just wearing it like a hat, then looks totally offended when we laugh.
my Rottweiler would always come curl up in my lap whenever I would sit down crisscross applesauce. She did that until she was 12 when she passed away

Have a golden lab, around 60kg, 7 years old. Genuinely wants carried like a baby, will sit on your knee with his paws on your shoulders. Had a black lab before and just tolerated hugs, never looked for them, this brute will cry/whine till he's on your lap. If he gets the chance to sleep next to you, he sleeps on you, cutting off most blood circulation. Worth it? Every. Single. Time.
Omg...golden mixes are adorable! Goldendoodle person here! Tucker does the same thing...he's try and get right on your lap; he's around eighty pounds...and two years old.
Yes, but probably because after six years I still call him Puppy as a nickname. 🤷‍♂️
My 75ish lb coonhound thinks he's wee little. Has no idea he's a 9 year old wrecking ball
Yes, my J. My "twins" are 10 years old. L. acts like a grown dog, but J. has never grown up. She gets ultra-excited and speeds around like a maniac when I offer her a treat.
my 90lb lab insists on sleeping in a cardboard box meant for a kitten. he just sits there, looking proud and cramped. it's hilarious but also kinda sad? lol
Yeah mine is almost 5 and he still hasn't calmed down. I've an active dog ( English pointer) no surprise to me though 😅
Mine still tries to sit on my lap and she's pushing 30kg. My ribs never stood a chance.

just adopted a year old dog a few days ago. so he’s not all the way grown but he weighs 50 lbs and he is completely unaware of that fact. he’s so so gentle taking treats but he jumps on everyone. once i was laying on the couch and he jumped on me and nailed me right in the nose. now i sit up when he approaches me. he is a wrecking ball and i love him
my 7-year old Rottweiler is a total puppy. wants to play all the time. best characterized as a happy frat boy.
My 105 lbs giant has zero comprehension of his size. He looks at a barking chihuahua like it’s a bear and hides behind my legs. He also stands on my feet and doesn’t understand why it would hurt.

I think I don't help my baby when I baby him all the time. He's now 4 but I do baby him a lot. I can't help it. He's a chihuahua so I guess that small dog syndrome kinda makes sense but boy do I show him he's a baby!

Mine did this until the day he died, so over ten years. By the time he was full grown, he was a solid 70 pounds with no fat on him.

ETA: he would cry so often and whine just to have every ounce of attention when I was on the phone. If I wasn’t on the phone, perfectly content beside me. When I was on the phone, immediate whine for attention. He was a GSP and Pitt mix.
I've had lap dogs up to about 130lbs, some don't ever grow out of that lol

My 80lb pittie will bodyslam me when she find a good spot in the bed next to me or she will stand on my stomach to get my attention. When I sit on the couch she must climb up and place herself on my lap. Granted, she's only two years old
